Application rates have been reduced to a range of 250-350 pounds per lane mile per pass in 1974 (as opposed to 300-400 pounds per lane mile per pass in 1973) on the primary system of roadways (approximately 1,700 miles), and to a range of 350-450 pounds per lane mile pass on the expressways system of roadways (approximately 260 miles) within the District. The spreaders used on the expressways are calibrated for 400 pounds per lane mile and those used on the primary system are calibrated for 300 pounds per lane mile.
D. Erosion
The contractors will be responsible for the area of raw, erodible earth exposed at any time. Erosion should be avoided by sodding or seeding of exposed areas or by the use of mulch or matting. Since the reconstruction of Lincoln Highway is mainly a widening of the existing roadway, erosion and subsequent sedimentation problems should be minimal. A copy of the special provisions for temporary project water pollution control concerning erosion is included in this report as Appendix D.
E. Drainage Considerations
A closed drainage system will be built along the entire proposed improvement. The improvement of this highway will maintain present drainage patterns in accordance with the provisions and limitations established by the General Assembly of the State of Illinois, and contained in the Illinois Revised Statutes.
In the interest of the general public who are faced with increased flooding due to urbanization, every effort will be made to control run-off from the highway right-of-way. (See Appendix "E" excerpts from the Illinois Highway Drainage Policy and Practice Manual).
